name: The Steppe
text: [overview] Depending on the year, expect WI1-2 ice or only snow.

name: Crossbow
text: [approach] A short bushwhack leads into a narrow snow gully, followed by a few hundred feet of snow to the first ice.

name: East Gully
text: [overview] Snow gully in King Ravine, on the left, among the lengthier lines there, topping out marginally above Iced Out Gully.
[overview] Follow it until the footing cleans up higher, then take steeper snow with fine views to the top.

name: Great Gully
text: [overview] Depending on snow depth, expect possible brush thrashing at the start.
[overview] Mostly moderate snow low down;
[overview] an ice bulge, possibly large, may form around a third of the way up, avoidable via a snowfield on climber's left.
[overview] Snow in the top third steepens to roughly 45 degrees, then flattens out close to Thunderstorm Junction, above treeline.
[detailed_rack] Pickets, and maybe screws.
[approach] From the ravine floor follow the Great Gully trail, if you can find it under the snow, to the foot of the gully, which is hard to miss.
[approach] Expect to push through brush at the bottom when the snow is thin.

name: Iced Out Gully
text: [overview] Leave the bushes on moderate snow with some small ice steps, cross easy-angled talus, and meet the hiking trails to descend.

name: Up the Creek Without a Paddle
text: [overview] this stretch is a miserable bushwhack in early season, and big snow years may make it easier.
[overview] A snow step of about 30 ft at 55 degrees leads to top out through a brief chimney/boulder section, and the ridge then carries you out of the ravine.

name: Middle Sister
text: [detailed_rack] pickets or rock protection can be carried if wanted.

name: North Sister
text: [what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons

name: South Sister
text: [overview] Leave the sisters' common runout, break left over a bush terrace, and go up the broad snow gully;

name: Central Couloir
text: [overview] A gully of snow and ice, over 1000' long, ends at the buttress dividing Central from Green Chasm, where it bends sharply left.
[overview] Past that bend the snow continues to a big, steep flow at the back (WI 3+/4+).

name: Horseshoe Gully
text: [overview] Starts as a shallow streambed gully, then gains several pleasant WI1-2 ice steps with snowfields in between.

name: Landslide Gully
text: [overview] Depending on conditions, approach over snow or talus to reach the first ice.
[descent_text] That trail is very steep, so crampons may be useful.

name: Shoestring Gully
text: [overview] It begins as easy snow among boulders and, after about 1000 ft, tightens and steepens between confined walls.
[overview] With typical snowfall, pitches are only a quarter to a third ice, with steep snow making up the remainder.
[detailed_rack] A few screws, and snow pickets perhaps, depending on conditions.
[approach] Snow or rock leads up for several hundred vertical feet to the first ice.
[descent_text] It is one of the steepest trails in the range, so crampons may be needed.

name: Brad White's Route One "Long Way Home"
text: [approach] This remote north-facing area is reached from the Lincoln Woods parking lot: cross the Kancamagus Highway and head straight into the woods on snowshoes, over open, easy snow bushwhacking, to the frozen cascades.

name: Monroe Brook Slide
text: [overview] Climb conifer glades into the slide, then follow easy snow to its end.
[overview] Usual northwest winds likely scour it, ideal for crampons.
[approach] Leave the trail there on your right, climb through open conifer glades to the foot of the slide, then follow the easy snow gully uphill.
[approach] Snow here is often scoured by wind, so crampons are useful.

name: South Branch
text: [overview] South Gully is bush-lined, climbs steep snow, topping a convex roll, and opens into a vast snowfield.
[detailed_rack] if cautious on a very firm day, bring pickets, since bushes and open water make long slides worse.

name: Central Gully
text: [overview] most of it is snow at a steeper angle.
[overview] Ice difficulty varies widely with snow cover, from easy up to about 2 or 2+ when snow is thin and conditions are cold and wet.

[descent_text] From there you can go back down the gully if you are comfortable on the steep snow, or head left along the Alpine Garden to the Escape Hatch, or follow the Lion Head Trail south along the Alpine Garden, which is the more scenic choice.

name: Damnation Gully
text: [overview] It tops out right on the north wall's rim, sometimes under a small cornice.
[approach] Crampon up the steepening snow into the deep, narrow gully;
[descent_text] Near the top the gully forks, and bearing left through snow and frozen turf reaches the lip of the ravine, while a cornice can build on the direct line.

name: Diagonal Gully
text: [overview] A long, nearly straight snow gully that runs almost to the lip of the ravine.
[overview] It is an acceptable snow climb but more often used as a quick descent to the floor of the ravine.
[detailed_rack] Maybe a few ice screws for the ice bulge at the base, and snow pickets if desired.

name: North Gully
text: [overview] After that comes what felt like 1,000 feet of snow at 60-80 degrees.
[detailed_rack] Small ice rack plus snow protection.

name: Odell's Gully
text: [overview] Plenty of low-angle snow above makes it especially avalanche-prone;

name: Pinnacle Gully
text: [approach] Most trouble on this route comes from the snow above the ice, so check the avalanche forecast before you go.

name: South gully
text: [overview] A fine snow route with a modest ice step midway, and a decent substitute for Central Gully.
[detailed_rack] Carry an axe, a pair of snow pickets and ice screws for extra security.
[approach] Take the clear snow ramp along the far-left side of the fan below the headwall.

name: Yale Gully
text: [overview] A long snow slope leads to the Harvard ice bulge, a full rope length: easier toward the right, somewhat steeper toward the left.
[overview] Easy snow then gives onto the gully itself, a shallow one.
[overview] Snow cover decides what comes next: more ice bulges, rocky scrambling that is loose, or just snow.
[detailed_rack] A few screws, perhaps plus some rock gear and pickets.
[approach] Begin up a long snow slope to a rope-length ice bulge.

name: Summer Slide
text: [detailed_rack] Ice screws and maybe one or two snow pickets.

name: The Chute
text: [approach] snowshoes are needed once you leave the packed Signal Ridge trail.

name: Boott Spur Gully
text: [overview] Its aspect means less wind loading, so the ice bulges stay unburied, a challenge for skiers but potentially a pleasant objective, short pitches over the bulges (WI1-2) with simul-climbing on the snow.
[overview] The largest ice bulges come first, then long stretches of Moderate Snow mixed with ice slabs.
[detailed_rack] Some screws, a light rope, and possibly a picket.
[approach] the biggest ice bulge comes first, then long sections of snow.

name: Cathedral Gully
text: [overview] Take the brushy approach gully used for Stovepipe, over bushes, snow and bare talus, and choose the left of two gullies (the right is Stovepipe).
[detailed_rack] Pickets if the snow is firm or the exposure worries you.
[approach] The approach goes through bushes, snow and bare talus, and then you enter a high-walled couloir.

name: Chute, The
text: [overview] Kick straight up the steep snow, reaching 50 degrees high up, where the last steps roll over to nearly flat, a blind top-out famous for unnerving skiers.
[detailed_rack] pickets can serve as running protection on the steeper parts.
[approach] All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.
[descent_text] A slip here can slide a long way, so be sure of your axe and crampons.

name: Dodge's Drop
text: [detailed_rack] Bring pickets, plus a few screws when ice is present;
[descent_text] a cornice near the top may need working around.

name: Hillman's Highway
text: [overview] The broad snow gully above steepens halfway and divides;
[detailed_rack] In firm conditions, pickets can protect pitches on the steeper sections.
[approach] Follow the wide snow gully uphill.

name: Left Gully
text: [approach] Rock walls line it, and it is mostly easy snow.
[approach] All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.
[descent_text] The gully finishes under a headwall that can be steep snow or a large cornice;
[descent_text] From there Right Gully or Lobster Claw give easy snow back into the ravine, or take the Lion Head Winter Route to the Tuckerman Ravine Trail.

name: Lion's Head Gully
text: [overview] From there cross to the East Snowfields for the summit, or descend.
[overview] Big snow years make it skiable.
[approach] All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.
[descent_text] The gully ends at the Alpine Garden, from which you can cross to the summit by the East Snowfields.

name: Lip, The
text: [overview] mid to late winter brings skiing and steep snow.
[overview] Climb the steep face to the right of the Icefall from the ravine floor;
[overview] Beyond a convex roll the angle eases, with easy access to Washington's East Snowfields.
[overview] Spring brings huge glide cracks, with snow undermined;
[detailed_rack] Pickets suit firm snow, and ice screws are needed for early-season ice, which varies greatly year to year.
[approach] The Lip is the obvious steep snow face just to the right of the big central icefall on the headwall.
[approach] All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.
[descent_text] The steep face eases to low-angle snow with easy access to the East Snowfields.
[descent_text] Glide cracks and undermined snow can form late in the season, and the area may be closed then, so follow any signs.

name: Lobster Claw
text: [overview] Snow gully on the ravine's right wall, named for its outline as seen from Boott Spur.
[approach] All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.

name: Right Gully
text: [overview] Expect crowds, nice snow and good views.
[overview] Aim for the broad gully mid-way along the ravine's right wall, skirting shrubs and boulders, then climb straightforward snow up to the Alpine Garden.
[overview] From there the summit is simple, over the East Snowfields or by the hiking routes.
[approach] the snow above is straightforward.
[approach] All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.
[descent_text] The gully reaches the Alpine Garden, with the summit reachable by the East Snowfields or hiking trails.

name: Side Chute
text: [approach] Side Chute leaves Dodge's Drop about halfway up, on the right, through a steep rock pinch before moderate snow.

name: Sluice Ice
text: [overview] Ascend the snow gully to the foot of the obvious ice, place a screw to secure the belayer, then work up the ice flows rated WI3+ to WI4 to snow higher up, belaying from ice where possible.
[overview] Continue in pitches up the steep snow, stopping once a walk-off feels safe.
[detailed_rack] Ice screws, perhaps pickets.
[approach] Go up the snow gully to the ice, then place a screw to anchor your belayer.
[approach] All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.
[descent_text] Keep pitching the steep snow above the ice until you are comfortable walking.

name: Stovepipe
text: [overview] Climb steep snow until rocks stop it.
[overview] mid to late winter snow usually covers everything.
[detailed_rack] Pickets for the steep snow.
[detailed_rack] if snowy, pickets help when firm or if exposure worries you.
[descent_text] in early season this is easy scrambling on talus up to the ridge, and in mid to late winter it is usually all snow.

name: The Byrds
text: [overview] Snow follows, moderate then steep, and the finish weaves through rocky outcrops.

name: The Open Book
text: [detailed_rack] Pickets suit a snow-covered top.
[approach] All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow slopes, so check the avalanche forecast, and expect skiers above if you descend on foot.
[descent_text] If snow has buried the trail, continue up and right to the Alpine Garden and descend Right Gully or the Lion Head Winter Route.
